title: close, start and host-check still write an upstream sprint, and intake and red-pipeline can change upstream items
goal: every backlog.py command that writes an item or sprint file refuses one that arrived from the clone's upstream main, the commands that take a sprint (close, start, host-check) included, reading the id from the argument each command takes; intake and red-pipeline never change an upstream item; backlog.md's provenance section lists the refusing commands as the code has them

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import backlog;m=[c for c in ('close','start') if c not in backlog.UPSTREAM_WRITERS];print('sprint writers outside the upstream guard:',m);sys.exit(1 if m else 0)

repro_reason: the full defect needs a throwaway clone with an upstream holding a sprint (the SP-3trnelzv review ran it: host-check wrote host_checked into an upstream item, close deleted an upstream sprint); the repro reads the guard's command list, and the fix's check must plant that clone

run:
import json,os,subprocess as S,sys,tempfile
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0,'_tools')
import backlog
T=Path(backlog.__file__).resolve().parent;t=Path(tempfile.mkdtemp());e=dict(os.environ,GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='t',GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL='t@example.com',GIT_COMMITTER_NAME='t',GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL='t@example.com')
g=lambda *a,cwd:S.run(['git',*a],cwd=cwd,capture_output=True,text=True,env=e)
b=lambda r,*a:(lambda p:(p.returncode,p.stdout+p.stderr))(S.run([sys.executable,str(T/'backlog.py'),'--root',str(r),*a],cwd=r,capture_output=True,text=True,env=e))
u=t/'up';u.mkdir();g('init','-q','-b','main',cwd=u)
(u/'backlog.json').write_text(json.dumps({'item_dir':'items','id_prefixes':{'story':'ST','bug':'BG','sprint':'SP'}}))
sp=b(u,'new','sprint','--title','s','--goal','g')[1].split()[2]
it=b(u,'new','story','--title','i','--sprint',sp,'--touch','x','--goal','g')[1].split()[2]
g('add','-A',cwd=u);g('commit','-qm','p',cwd=u)
c=t/'clone';g('clone','-q','-o','upstream',str(u),str(c),cwd=t);g('config','kb.upstreamRemote','upstream',cwd=c)
f=lambda:{p.name:p.read_bytes() for p in (c/'items').glob('*.json')}
was=f();m=[]
for a in (['close',sp],['start',sp],['host-check',sp],['land',it]):
    r,o=b(c,*a)
    if r!=1 or 'arrived from the upstream main' not in o:m.append(a[0])
b(c,'fmt')
print('upstream sprint/item writers not refused:',m,'| upstream files changed:',f()!=was)
sys.exit(1 if m or f()!=was else 0)

gates.question: Where does the sprint-writer refusal live: backlog.py extends bl_base's UPSTREAM_WRITERS tuple, or bl_base's tuple itself changes?

How do intake and red-pipeline keep an upstream item unchanged, and what else joins the guard: an upstream near-duplicate or fingerprint match is skipped as a merge target so the clone files its own draft or bug, or the finding is dropped?
options: skip upstream matches as merge targets, file own; fmt skips upstream files; land joins the guard
drop the finding when an upstream item matches
gates.recommendation: skip upstream matches as merge targets, file own; fmt skips upstream files; land joins the guard
gates.answer: skip upstream matches as merge targets, file own; fmt skips upstream files; land joins the guard

notes: 2026-10-24: _tools/bl_close.py left out of the touches, since workhorse's ST-55ueywel holds it: the close and start refusal goes in backlog.py's guard (the UPSTREAM_WRITERS check reads a sprint argument as well as an item id), not in bl_close.py.
